resources.instruction: Write tests by observable behaviour (an input leading to a result or a data state), not by implementation. Each acceptanceCriteria has at least one test; name a test after the behaviour (for example "rejects an empty title"), do not use the AC code. Choose the narrowest test that proves the behaviour: unit first, integration when the behaviour crosses a boundary. Each test is independent, does not depend on order, cleans up its own data, and gives a deterministic result (no dependence on the clock, random order, the network). Use the repository's existing test utilities and sample data.

Cover error paths and boundary values: every operation that has a success path has tests for wrong input (missing, empty, only whitespace, too long, wrong type), boundary values (exactly at the allowed limit and one unit over it), objects that do not exist, and conflicts (duplicates). Check the returned error code or message too, not just "there is an error". Confirm the error leaves no side effects (no half-written record). Do not write a test only to raise coverage without asserting anything.
